findings.F1: The book loses because fees take more than the trades gain: summed over all coins and windows, the gain before costs is +0.295 while fees are 0.396, so the book ends at −0.101. The fees fall almost entirely at entry and exit, 0.199 on Sunday's entry bar and 0.179 on Tuesday's exit bars, against less than 0.02 on all other days.
findings.F2: The Monday–Tuesday hold itself pays: its gain before costs sums to +0.822 (Monday +0.081, Tuesday +0.741). Per case it is +0.122 % of the book over the 48 bars, with t 0.84 over 563 cases. Each case's entry and exit fees are about 0.072 % of the book. So the hold nets roughly +0.05 % per case before what happens after it.
findings.F3: 18.8 % of cases still hold a short after the 48 bars, and the book is short on about 12 % of all Wednesday-to-Sunday bars. Those bars lose −0.526 in summed gain, which is about two thirds of the Monday–Tuesday gain. The 86 trades held over 200 hours average −4.24 % each before fees.
findings.F4: The reversal is almost all on Tuesday. The book was short on a similar share of bars both days (27.7 % Monday, 26.9 % Tuesday), but Tuesday's summed gain is +0.741 against Monday's +0.081.
findings.F5: The size of the forecast does not grade the fall. Across the quartiles of the forecast's size, the 48-bar coin return after the signal runs −0.30 %, −0.97 %, +0.69 %, −1.78 %, not a steady rise in the fall. The step-5 check of the larger half minus the smaller half is −0.08 %. The forecast standardises the weekend's 48-bar gain over only 60 hourly bars, so it compares the weekend mostly with itself.
findings.F6: The effect exists and is large per case: an unusual fall of +0.84 % over 48 bars (strength 0.118, t 2.80, 557 cases), against a 0.19 % cost per trade. But it is earned against the coin's normal drift (−0.27 % in the short's direction), and the book is short only, with a mean position of −0.39 of the book at entry.

ideas.idea: When a coin's price rises from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC, it falls over the following two days, only while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its own last 6 months, and the larger the weekend gain against the coin's usual two-day move over the last 30 days, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the Monday fade by how unusual the weekend's rise is for that coin's recent two-day moves, putting more of the book on the rare large weekend rises, where the fall pays the most against the fixed fee per trade.
ideas.name: weekend rise against usual moves

ideas.idea: When a coin's price rises from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC, it falls over the following two days, only while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its own last 6 months, with the larger part of the fall coming on Tuesday, the second day, and the larger the weekend gain, the larger Tuesday's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the fade through Tuesday and judge its result on the second day, not on Monday's move.
ideas.name: weekend reversal lands Tuesday

ideas.idea: When a coin's price rises from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC, it falls over the following two days, only while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its own last 6 months, and from Wednesday over the next five days it returns to rising with its normal drift, the more so the larger the weekend gain was.
ideas.consequence: A trader would close the fade by Tuesday's end and carry no short past it, since shorts held into the rest of the week give back most of what the two days earned.
ideas.name: reversal ends after Tuesday
